name: Deep Terracotta
lede: Deep Terracotta is a dark, burnt orange-red close to the fired clay it is named for, and close to a hue Werner's 1821 nomenclature of colours called "Tile Red".

sections.title: Older than the modifier grammar
sections.body:
The nearest named colors on file are [[copper-red]], [[adobe]] and [[signal-orange]], at 3, 3.3 and 4.1 ΔE [1]. Its ISCC-NBS block reads "moderate reddish orange" [1].

The closest match among older sources is plate 82 of Patrick Syme's 1821 edition of Werner's nomenclature of colours, "Tile Red", illustrated there with the breast of the cock bullfinch, shrubby pimpernel and porcelain jasper [2]. Werner's book predates the modern name by 189 years; the resemblance is of hue, not of name [2]. [[bright-terracotta|Bright Terracotta]], [[brick|Brick]] and [[rust|Rust]] sit nearby in our library [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Deep Terracotta covers at least 2% of the canvas in 231 of our 23,781 paintings, and by position in each painting's lightness order it is found in 205, more common than 71% of the named colors we track, as photographed [3]. It is most often an accent, the role in 91% of those matched paintings, and is most over-represented in paintings from India, at 3.2 times the expected rate [3].

The earliest match is the year 1000, 821 years before Werner's 1821 "Tile Red" and 821 years before the modern name, which again says only that a similar hue was photographed there, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3].

origin.source: Syme, Werner's Nomenclature of Colours, 2nd ed. (1821), plate 82
